prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1204; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a low-speed collision while backing out of a space in a parking lot and said the other vehicle struck the rear quarter panel of their car. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and provided initial contact details voluntarily.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the incident, as the responding officer and two witnesses described the same sequence of events.

Entry 3: Obtained photos from the scene and from the other driver showing contact damage consistent with the described impact. The damage to the rear quarter panel and bumper is mostly in line with a collision of this type.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the accident happened as the claimant described it and that the vehicles made contact in the lot.

Entry 5: Claimant reports pain in the right shoulder following the impact and has started seeing a physician. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this kind.

Entry 6: Checked prior claims and vehicle history. No earlier damage to this vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of the current coverage period.

Entry 7: Confirmed no earlier injury to the same shoulder area is on file. Claimant described no prior treatment for that body part.

Entry 8: Claimant told the same account of the incident in each conversation so far, including the location, the direction of travel, and the sequence of contact.

Entry 9: Received treatment records showing the claimant attended physical therapy on a usual schedule. Symptoms have improved steadily, and the treatment plan is tapering off as recovery progresses.

Entry 10: Confirmed the driver of the vehicle lives with the policyholder and qualifies as a covered household member under the policy.

Entry 11: Reviewed the medical notes with the claimant's permission. Progress is consistent with the expected recovery course for this type of soft tissue shoulder injury, and no complications have been recorded.

Entry 12: Claim is progressing normally. Remaining items are the final medical bill and the repair estimate. Will follow up once both are received.
